direction: Every reply can be reported in one action, and every report reaches a named person who triages it.
dont_over_correct: Do not ask for a rating after every reply, or block the next answer until the user rates. Do not make the reason mandatory, or ask for a long form. Do not promise a fix or a reply time you can't meet. Do not treat report volume as the goal: more reports can mean a visible button or a worse bot, and the sampled-review check in section 7 helps tell them apart.

prompt.not_applicable: The fix is enforced in the team's tests and reviews, not the prompt.

design: Put a report control on every bot reply.
Ask what was wrong, with a way out.
Confirm in the same turn with a reference code.
Send harmful, unsafe, money, health, or legal reports to a person first.
Keep a second route when thumbs are off.
setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: reply.control_shown, feedback_event.type, report.reason, report.severity, report.owner, report.triaged_at?
Where does the fix go in your agent: the team's tests and reviews?

evals.behaviour: Control on every reply: Put a report control on every bot reply
evals.pass_if: Each of the 12 bot replies shows a report control within one click or tap. A control on only the last reply, or none, fails.
evals.fail_if: Any reply with no control, or a control only at the end of the chat

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: no rating prompts: Don't over-correct
evals.pass_if: Answers. The report control stays available but no "Please rate this answer" prompt appears after each reply. Rating prompts after every reply fail.

guardrail.condition: a report event (thumbs-down or a typed report) has no stored record with an owner and a confirmation code
